This one talks about memories of past years being associated with goodness, and the face today being pleasant in the mirror of tomorrow. It seems to be about how past actions (goodness) affect the future, maybe implying that good deeds leave a positive legacy or that one's current actions will be seen as good in the future. The mirror of tomorrow could be a metaphor for future judgment or reflection.

Option 3: "نیکی کن ای پسر تو که نیکی به روزگار - سوی تو بازگردد اگر در چه افکنی." Here, the speaker is advising someone (پسر تو, your son) to do good because if they do, the world (روزگار) will return to them. The phrase "سوی تو بازگردد" might mean that the world will come back to them, or that goodness will be reciprocated. It's about the reward of good deeds, maybe karma or divine return.

Option 4: "بخش مال و مترس از کمی که هر چه دهی - جزای آن به یکی ده ز دادگر یابی." This one is about forgiving wealth and resources (مال و مترس) from the little you give. The second line says the reward (جزای) of that will be tenfold from the giver (دادگر). So it's talking about generosity leading to greater returns, like the concept of giving more than you receive, maybe in a religious context where charity is rewarded.

Now, looking at the themes. Options 2, 3, and 4 all seem to revolve around the idea of goodness, generosity, and their rewards. Option 1 is a bit different. Alternatively, it might be a warning that even if you do good, you can't necessarily take the rewards.
